subject: ZenithWorks MSA/DPA: integration scope, SLA carveouts, and data residency appendix

Subject: Draft MSA/DPA for integration

Diego,

Thanks again for the call earlier — excited about the integration between ZenithWorks connectors and Redwood's inference endpoints. My legal team attached a redlined MSA + DPA (Zenith_Integra_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf) and a draft SOW that scopes the initial connector work. High level asks from our side:

- Narrow the warranty language to exclude third-party data transformation steps.
- Add an SLA carveout for pre-production spikes caused by customer-driven load testing.
- Add a data residency appendix for EU-hosted tenants (we'll propose specific language in a follow-up).

Can you confirm who at Redwood will handle commercial redlines vs. legal redlines? We'd like to move to an exec-signed agreement this month if possible.

Attachments: Zenith_Integra_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf, SOW-ZW-Integration-v1.docx

Subject: Re: Draft MSA/DPA for integration

Aisha — thanks for sending. I reviewed the redlines at a high level and looped in Monica (legal) and Rishi (commercial). Quick notes from a commercial standpoint:

- We can accept a carveout for intentional customer load tests but need a clear definition ("scheduled load test with prior notice") and a cap on impact to SLA credits.
- Warranty scope: agreeable to narrower warranty but will push back on language that could create a broad IP indemnity.
- Data residency appendix: we want to keep the appendix simple — confirm which workloads (inference only? logs?) you expect to be EU-resident.

Internal ask: Monica/Rishi — can you review the attached redlines and suggest a counter that keeps our standard liability cap and preserves fallback routing for cross-region requests?

I'll propose a short sync this week with ZenithWorks legal if that helps.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Draft MSA/DPA for integration

Diego — I reviewed Zenith's redlines (see attached internal markup: data-residency-appendix-draft.pdf with comments). Summary of recommended positions and trade-offs:

1) SLA carveouts and credits
- We accept a defined carveout for customer-initiated load tests (>10x baseline for more than 30 minutes) provided Zenith commits to a 72-hour advance notice and agrees not to count those windows toward uptime calculations.
- Proposed language: "Scheduled performance testing (notified >72 hours in advance) shall be excluded from SLA uptime calculations; unplanned spikes remain subject to standard SLA remedy."

2) Warranty / IP indemnity
- Do not agree to language that removes our warranty cap or broadens indemnity to cover third-party code. Counter: keep existing cap at contract value (12 months of fees) and add explicit carveout for third-party transformation steps.

3) Data residency appendix
- Zenith asks for "EU-resident logs" — we can commit to EU inference processing for specified tenant IDs, but logs for system telemetry/live debugging will be retained in the region needed to operate routing and support (30 days). If Zenith requires 90-day regional log retention, we need an uplift to cover storage costs or an enterprise add-on.

4) SOW scoping / acceptance criteria
- Keep acceptance tied to a joint test plan and three acceptance scenarios (connectivity, throughput at X TPS, and correct semantic mapping). Avoid ambiguous language like "works as expected."

Negotiation strategy: hold firm on liability cap + telemetry carveout; offer a pricing uplift or extended retention as a commercial concession. Rishi, can you draft a short pricing amendment we can use as a lever?

Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MSA/DPA for integration

Thanks Monica and Diego — appreciate the clarity. A few counterpoints from our legal team:

- Zenith can accept the scheduled-testing carveout language but requests the notice window be 48 hours instead of 72.
- On data residency: we are specifically asking that inference request payloads and generated outputs for EU-tenant IDs remain in EU data centers for the lifecycle of the transaction; logs related to request routing may be permitted to cross-region for debugging but must be scrubbed of PII within 24 hours.
- Regarding liability cap: our VP engineering is uncomfortable with a cap equal to 12 months of fees for this integration (given potential downstream revenue). Would Redwood consider liability tied to actual damages without punitive? Alternatively, increase the cap to 24 months of fees for integration-related claims.

Action items from Zenith: we can do a one-hour call to resolve the remaining items. Also attaching a clean SOW with scope tweaks (SOW-ZW-Integration-v1.docx).

Subject: Re: Draft MSA/DPA for integration — proposed path forward

Aisha / team — thanks for the thoughtful responses and for being flexible on several points. Quick summary and next steps to align teams and keep to our November close target: 

Agreed positions:
- SLA carveout: Redwood accepts scheduled testing carveout with a 72-hour notice. Zenith prefers 48 hours; we propose 72 hours as the compromise that protects customers while still being operationally reasonable.
- Data residency: Redwood will commit to EU processing for inference payloads and generated outputs for tenant IDs flagged as EU (appendix will list tenant IDs and obligations). Telemetry/logs used for routing/observability will be stored for 30 days by default; Zenith may purchase extended 90-day EU-only log retention as an add-on.
- Liability cap: Redwood will keep the standard cap (12 months of fees) but will agree to a carveout for willful misconduct. We are not prepared to move to a 24-month cap without commercial uplift.

Next steps and owners:
- Monica to deliver final legal counter (clean MSA + tracked DPA) by Wed 11/11.
- Rishi to prepare a short commercial amendment that offers a pricing uplift option for 90-day EU log retention and an optional 24-month liability cap (deal-specific fee).
- Diego to schedule a 60-minute legal/commercial sync with ZenithWorks (Aisha + Mark + Zenith legal). Proposed times: Wed 11/11 09:00-11:00 PT or Thu 11/12 10:00-12:00 PT. Please confirm availability.

Attachments: SOW-ZW-Integration-v1.docx (updated with acceptance criteria), data-residency-appendix-draft.pdf

If we can get Monica's counter and Rishi's amendment by Wednesday, we can aim to have exec signatures the following week.
